tagline: Ranch-To-Table Cuisine Has Arrived to Danville
cuisine: Mexican / Californio "rancho cuisine" — wood-fired grill, tequila & mezcal bar
description: Rancho Cantina Danville is the second location of the family-owned Lafayette original, opened by longtime Danville residents Nico and Alice Tzikas in the former Cocina Hermanas building on the corner of Hartz Avenue and Church Street. The kitchen, led by Executive Chef Carlos Navarro, cooks over a wood-fired (almond wood) grill and describes its food as inspired by the Spanish-Mexican Californios of California's ranching era: Vaquero Platters, carne asada, brick chicken, a 32 oz Cowboy Cut ribeye, and whole fried branzino alongside tacos, enchiladas, burritos and sizzling fajita skillets. The larger Danville building allowed a more substantial bar built around tequila and mezcal cocktails and a five-margarita lineup, with outdoor seating on the Hartz Avenue corner. It soft-opened Monday, August 24, 2026, with full online reservations from September 1.

owner_chef: Owners: Nico and Alice Tzikas (Danville residents; took over the Lafayette original in April 2024). Executive Chef: Carlos Navarro (credited on the Danville printed menu).
opened: Soft opened Monday, August 24, 2026; full online reservations from September 1, 2026 (Bay Area Telegraph). Diablo Dish dates the soft opening as August 26, 2026.
brand_colors_or_style: Squarespace site with a restrained, heritage-serif look: headings in Orpheus Pro (a high-contrast display serif) and body/meta text in Adobe Garamond Pro; palette is black and white with a dark espresso-brown accent (hsl 42° 42% 13%, approx #2E2613) used for buttons/links and a pale warm gray (hsl 210° 3% 88%) secondary; page sections alternate white and black backgrounds. The printed menu is set on khaki/beige stock with a thin bracket-framed "RANCHO CANTINA" serif wordmark in black, gold-tan section headings (ANTOJITOS, WOOD FIRED, MARGARITA TIME), small crown ornaments, and vintage line-art illustrations of a vaquero on horseback, a covered wagon, a whole fish, a cowboy hat and a skillet. The Danville storefront was repainted in a medium tan body with a burnt-orange secondary and off-white trim (Bay Area Telegraph). Overall mood: rustic old-California ranch / Californio heritage rather than bright cantina kitsch.
